assumptions.summary: Screened and imputed data are treated as correct and robust for later analysis.
The four states' natural resources remain abundant and are not exhausted before 2050.
After 2009 all energy types are treated as identical in total production-plus-environmental cost.
Inflation/GDP-deflator behavior is treated as unchanged in future years.
The analysis focuses on macroeconomy and energy structure, especially renewable and clean energy.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The source describes fifty years and 605 variables for Arizona, California, New Mexico and Texas.
Integrity/usefulness screening is followed by cointegration and MDS narrowing.
Repeated zeros may be missing or genuine zero use; mean substitution is selected after that caveat.
Data are classified by usage, source, sector and environmental impact.
Fossil average price is corrected to reduce local extraction advantage.
Ten external-cost rates and five sector influence rates enter revised EROI.
Ten representative energy series are selected for dynamic fitting on 1970-2009 data.
Table 2 reports four-state 2025/2050 forecasts and two NaN category-state combinations.
Body tables report exact 2025/2050 clean-share and total-EROI targets.
Appendix code names external workbook dependencies but those files are not bundled in the PDF.

dependency_graph.handoff: Cleaned categories, prices and sectors feed revised EROI.
Screened historical factors feed the linear baseline.
Two baseline failures define the dynamic replacement's job.
The fitted dynamic system produces ten-category state forecasts.
No-policy level/share behavior triggers an incremental shock layer.
Policy simulations and state-only limits motivate compact duties.
Selected dynamic parameters feed the bounded sensitivity illustration.
EROI ranks and targets are cited in the action handoff.
Appendix functions consume the paper's cleaned-data and EROI interfaces.
Python code mirrors portions of EROI accounting; MATLAB mirrors entropy weighting.

independent_extensions.summary: Publish the 605-variable dictionary, screening decisions, cointegration tests, MDS settings and retained-set hashes.
Define a reproducible zero-versus-missing rule and compare imputation methods with uncertainty.
Audit all EIC/EEE units, base years, external-cost sources, sector rates and PEE lineage.
Evaluate linear, polynomial and dynamic baselines on one rolling-origin split with common metrics.
Release parameter estimates, expectation indexing, identifiability checks and convergence diagnostics.
Attach forecast intervals and preserve NaN or abstention when history is insufficient.
Calibrate shocks against observed interventions and separate demand, supply, fiscal and monetary costs.
Recompute the one-year/three-year comparison and reconcile the 200% versus half-better statements.
Model transmission capacity, losses, congestion, reliability, pipelines and state participation.
Expand sensitivity to ranges, fixed quantities, decision switches, active constraints and equilibrium loss.
Add construction cost, resource and technology constraints before treating targets as feasible.
Reconcile exact body targets with rounded memo values and release executable input workbooks/code.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The source refuses to call every zero missing before imputation.
A linear baseline is retained long enough to expose two specific failures.
Insufficient series remain NaN and absolute growth is distinguished from share decline.
The state-policy boundary explicitly motivates the interstate compact.
Three weaknesses precede exact body targets rather than being hidden after the memo.

language_observations.summary: Reusable human writing centers on ambiguity before repair, explicit unit/cost corrections, public baseline failure, bounded abstention, incremental shocks, level/share contrast, institution after state boundary and memo/body separation.
an unrealistic policy goal is narrowed to a reachable task: Turn broad aspiration into a decision output.
deliverables are ordered before methods: Give the reader a profile-to-action route.
manual screening precedes multivariate narrowing: Make compression respond to integrity and redundancy.
zero is not automatically treated as missing: Keep a domain alternative beside repair.
a repair is named after alternatives: Disclose the selected imputation route.
taxonomy follows imputation: Restore usage, source, sector and environmental meaning.
resource-price advantage is corrected before comparison: Prevent local extraction from masquerading as performance.
visual contrast triggers contextual explanation: Move from plant/profile differences to geography and industry.
a familiar ratio introduces a domain metric: Bridge financial ROI to energy return.
visible production cost is expanded by external harm: Make pollution enter the investment account.
unit mismatch triggers a conversion factor: Translate monetary investment into energy units.
nominal price rise is separated from real change: Make inter-year price comparison interpretable.
state and national prices form a geography factor: Turn local resource access into a formula input.
an external-cost table becomes a formula input: Prevent a literature table from remaining decorative.
sector impact contrast becomes an influence rate: Let use context alter environmental burden.
unlike use contexts receive separate equations: Distinguish end use from electric plants before aggregation.
component plots lead to a bounded state rank: Join end-use, plant and total EROI without collapsing them.
a failed prerequisite blocks a time-series model: Explain why ARMA/GARCH is not carried forward.
a linear baseline fails publicly before replacement: Make the dynamic model answer named failures.
an overfit patch is declined: Show why a local mathematical repair is insufficient.
redundancy is reduced to one series per energy category: Make dynamic inputs inspectable.
NaN is reported as an evidence boundary: Prevent unsupported development claims.
absolute growth is contrasted with declining share: Translate a forecast into a market-inertia problem.
shock terms enter only when policy becomes the question: Preserve a frozen forecast core and an incremental intervention layer.
a shock curve is narrated through phases: Turn a plot into an intervention horizon.
state-limited policy motivates a compact: Show why a cross-border institution becomes necessary.
analytical advice becomes formal obligations: Translate evidence into a negotiable compact.
sensitivity is stated with a narrow scope: Keep a one-parameter illustration from becoming a robustness claim.
process strengths and admitted limits use different roles: Separate self-evaluation from reopened interfaces.
exact target tables precede the action menu: Hand model outputs to policy without losing metric identity.
memo keeps current, future and action blocks: Translate evidence for governors.

results_trace.summary: In 2009 end-use clean/renewable shares are reported as 3.5% in Arizona, 2% in California and about 1% in New Mexico/Texas.
Reported 2009 total EROI is AZ 37.27%, CA 50.32%, NM 36.96% and TX 39.49%, ranking CA, TX, AZ, NM.
Arizona wind and New Mexico nuclear forecasts are NaN because of insufficient data.
The source reads the no-policy forecast as absolute growth for low-share energy but declining percentage share.
A demand shock is reported to jump immediately, dip next year, fluctuate for two more years and then decay.
The three-year versus one-year policy comparison contains internally awkward nearly-200% and nearly-half-better claims.
Body 2025 clean-share targets are AZ 40.64%, CA 42.90%, NM 36.69%, TX 35.47%.
Body 2050 clean-share targets are AZ 51.58%, CA 46.83%, NM 48.18%, TX 38.85%.
The memo rounds 2025 clean targets to about CA 42% and other states 35%, and compresses 2050 to a 38%-51% range.

unresolved_questions: The repeated red watermark is third-party page furniture and never author prose.
Contents entries and page-number leaders are excluded from positive language evidence.
Reference entries are source inventory, not author argumentative prose.
Python/MATLAB comments and code are implementation evidence, not positive prose.
The EIA plant map is a third-party visual asset; its labels are not author language.
The paper has a Summary sheet rather than a separately titled Abstract.
Type C is inherited from the parent directory, not inferred from title or content.
Manual screening criteria for integrity/usefulness are not completely enumerated.
Cointegration tests and MDS settings are not fully reported for all retained variables.
Equation (1) does not establish causality among screened variables.
Long runs of zeros may be missing observations or true zero use.
The rule used to distinguish missing zero from genuine zero is not reproducible from the text.
Mean substitution has no imputation-uncertainty analysis.
Classification by usage, source, sector and environmental impact may overlap.
Average fossil price is used to correct extraction advantage without a full market model.
State price differences can reflect regulation, transport and market structure, not only resource quality.
Population, industry and geography explanations are qualitative and noncausal.
The ROI-to-EROI analogy does not validate the selected output and investment proxies.
Total `EIC` is used as a proxy for energy yield based on asserted positive correlation.
The money-to-Btu conversion requires energy-intensity unit and year provenance.
The GDP-deflator correction freezes future inflation behavior by assumption.
Equation (4)’s price ratio is treated as resource quality without separate identification.
External-cost rates come from outside studies and require year/unit/applicability checks.
The ten external-cost numbers are not independently reproduced.
Sector influence rates are asserted rather than estimated in this paper.
`EIC`, `EEE`, inflation and sector weights can mix monetary and energy interpretations.
End-use and electric-plant boundaries can overlap without a published reconciliation table.
`PEE` lineage and units need explicit verification.
Total EROI is a model-defined composite, not a directly observed physical efficiency.
The 2009 state ranking has no confidence interval or alternative-weight sensitivity.
“California best” is conditional on the revised EROI definition and selected denominator.
End-use clean-energy shares and electric-generation shares must not be interchanged.
ADF failures are stated without a complete diagnostic table for every series.
The text alternates ARMA, ARCH and GARCH terminology; candidate boundaries need care.
Linear regressions are not compared under a single published holdout metric.
The polynomial-overfit concern is argued but not supported by a reported experiment.
The dynamic New Keynesian equations are adapted to energy variables with nonstandard economic meanings.
`i_t` is labeled energy ROI while `r_t` and `I` borrow monetary interest-rate language.
Several model parameters lack units, estimation intervals and identifiability checks.
The expectation-weight vector’s indexing and fitting procedure are incompletely documented.
The listed `α` weights sum to one but that alone does not validate expectations.
Selecting ten representative MSNs may discard category heterogeneity.
Parameter fitting on 1970–2009 lacks a documented train/validation split.
Table 2 forecasts are conditional trajectories, not probabilities or confidence intervals.
Arizona wind and New Mexico nuclear are `NaN` because of insufficient data.
Other non-`NaN` forecasts may still inherit short or unstable histories.
Absolute renewable growth can coexist with a declining share; the two metrics must remain separate.
The no-policy forecast assumes a policy environment the paper itself calls unrealistic.
Demand and supply shocks are stylized policy interfaces, not causal estimates.
The immediate-jump/oscillation/decay story is model behavior rather than observed intervention evidence.
The “nearly 200%” and “nearly half better” long-policy claims are internally awkward and must not be silently harmonized.
Supply shock, tax, subsidy, loan rate and construction effects are not costed on a common fiscal basis.
Interstate transmission and pipelines omit capacity, losses, congestion and reliability.
Technology investment lacks project selection, budget and monitoring rules.
The formal compact language does not establish legal authority or enforceability.
State obligations lack an implementation sequence and responsibility matrix.
Sensitivity varies only selected parameters in asserted ranges.
The Arizona natural-gas illustration is not a multivariate robustness study.
The sensitivity section does not report whether policy decisions switch.
Simplifying assumptions are admitted to create possible divergence.
Construction costs are omitted from the dynamic policy model.
Technology and resource constraints are omitted through 2050.
Many parameters can create local maxima/minima; no global certificate is supplied.
Author-listed strengths are process claims, not independent validation.
Body target tables and Summary/memo rounded targets are different source roles.
2025/2050 clean-share targets and total-EROI targets are different metrics.
The governor memo compresses evidence and cannot replace exact body tables.
Appendix code depends on external workbooks not frozen with this PDF.
Appendix code contains visibly garbled or truncated material and was not executed.
Original full-page PNGs stayed on disk; all eight review proxies are below 450,000 bytes and the bundle is below 4 MiB.

writing_logic.summary: far-fetched contract -> decision difficulty -> reasonable goals
profiles -> time behavior -> evaluation -> prediction -> actions
605 variables -> integrity/usefulness screen -> cointegration/MDS narrowing
zero run -> missing-or-real ambiguity -> distinguish -> mean substitution
resource-rich cheap price -> extraction advantage -> correction -> comparison
financial ROI -> energy analogue -> output/investment ratio
cheap production plus pollution harm -> EIC+EEE
currency investment -> energy-intensity bridge -> BTU account
nominal price rise -> dollar depreciation -> GDP-deflator correction
state/national price -> geography factor -> corrected cost
external-cost table -> ten groups -> denominator input
sector contrast -> influence rates -> end-use formula
end-use context -> plant context -> separate equations -> PEE-weighted total
component EROI views -> total metric -> 2009 state order
ADF prerequisite fails -> ARMA/GARCH rejected
linear baseline -> partial fit -> long/short failures -> dynamic replacement
polynomial patch -> overfit concern -> structural model
many factors -> redundancy -> one representative series per category
insufficient history -> NaN -> no fabricated development claim
absolute renewable growth -> declining share -> policy trigger
baseline dynamic system -> policy question -> shock-enhanced system
instant jump -> next-year dip -> short oscillation -> decay
state-only policy boundary -> transmission/technology/pipeline -> compact
WHEREAS evidence -> THEREFORE purpose -> EACH STATE SHALL duties
asserted economic range -> one state/fuel -> local sensitivity curve
process strengths -> omitted costs/resources/technology -> local-extrema warning
exact target tables -> subsidies, technology and infrastructure
current rank -> conditional future -> rounded goals -> compact actions
